newsitem.title: ITALY: BNL, INA interested in BankNapoli.
newsitem.headline: BNL, INA interested in BankNapoli.

text.p: Italy's state-controlled Banca Nazionale di Lavoro and insurer INA said on Monday they had formally expressed joint interest in Banco di Napoli.
A joint statement gave no further details. The Italian Treasury has put 60 percent of the struggling bank up for auction and interested parties have until December 20 to make offers.
Monday is the deadline for potential buyers to send a letter expressing interest in southern Italy's largest bank.
BNL president Mario Sarcinelli indicated to financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore on Sunday that if INA and BNL made a joint offer, INA would put up much of the cash and BNL would supply know-how.
INA is controlled by banks Istituto Bancario San Paolo Di Torino, IMI and Cariplo.

The BNL-INA bid is the only known expression of interest to date. Banco Ambrosiano Veneto and Banca Commerciale Italiano had previously indictated they might be interested in Banco di Napoli, but both groups have now said no.

Banco di Napoli unveiled record losses of 3.12 trillion lire ($2.0 billion) in 1995 and plunged a further 674 billion lire into the red in the first half of this year thanks largely to a poor, highly politicised loan policy.
The Treasury has installed new management at the firm and has promised to take on the vast bulk of the company's huge stock of bad debt before selling the group.

The European Commission has indicated to the Treasury that it wants Banco di Napoli to be sold by year end. If the auction fails to attract a buyer, the government might be forced to break up the bank and try to sell its various units separately.
